record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Classify all rational and elliptic cuspidal plane curves.

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 1. Classify all rational and elliptic cuspidal plane curves.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2 = \mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$. A reduced irreducible curve $C \subset \mathbb{P}^2$ is called cuspidal if every singular point of $C$ is a cusp, that is, a locally irreducible (unibranch) singularity. The geometric genus $g(C)$ is the genus of the normalization of $C$; $C$ is called rational if $g(C) = 0$ and elliptic if $g(C) = 1$.

Problem: Classify, up to projective equivalence (i.e. up to the action of $\mathrm{PGL}(3,\mathbb{C})$ on $\mathbb{P}^2$), all rational cuspidal plane curves and all elliptic cuspidal plane curves. Specifically, determine for each degree $d \geq 1$ and each prescribed collection of topological types of cusp singularities whether there exists such a curve $C \subset \mathbb{P}^2$ of degree $d$ with geometric genus $0$ (respectively $1$) realizing the prescribed cusps, and describe all such curves up to projective equivalence.
artifact.status_search_result: The full classification remains open. Substantial progress has been made: Koras and Palka proved that every rational cuspidal plane curve has at most four cusps via the almost minimal model program; complete classifications exist in special cases (e.g., rational unicuspidal curves with one Puiseux pair, by Fernández de Bobadilla–Luengo–Melle-Hernández–Némethi). However, a complete classification of rational (and elliptic) cuspidal plane curves of arbitrary degree and singularity type is still not achieved and is widely regarded as a difficult open problem.

status_evidence.title: On rational cuspidal projective plane curves
status_evidence.snippet: The classification of rational cuspidal curves, up to the action of PGL(3,C) on P^2, is a very difficult open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Classification of rational cuspidal plane curves is an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Rational Cuspidal Curves (Moe thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys partial classification results and lists open cases for rational cuspidal plane curves.

status_evidence.title: Classification of Rational Unicuspidal Projective Curves whose Singularities Have one Puiseux Pair
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a complete topological classification when C is unicuspidal with one Puiseux pair.

status_evidence.title: On free curves and related open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses recent results, including Koras–Palka bound of at most four cusps, and remaining open conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: Bounds and structural results known, full classification still open.
